content.intuition: Check every possible pair of numbers in the array to see if they sum to the target. This approach doesn't take advantage of the sorted property.
algorithm_steps: Use outer loop to iterate through each element
Use inner loop to check all elements after the current element
For each pair, check if their sum equals the target

time.explanation: Nested loops result in checking all possible pairs, leading to quadratic time complexity

space.explanation: Only using constant extra space for loop variables

why_suboptimal: Doesn't utilize the sorted property of the array
Checks unnecessary pairs that can't possibly sum to target
Time complexity is worse than the optimal O(n) solution
May time out on large inputs
when_to_use: When the array is not sorted (though hash map would be better)
As a starting point before optimization
For very small arrays where optimization doesn't matter
When demonstrating the importance of using data structure properties
interview_discussion_points: Why this approach works but is inefficient
How the sorted property can be leveraged
When brute force is acceptable vs when optimization is needed
